greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who invites us to knock at the door of heaven with confidence, be with you all.
penitential: Lord, you are the Father who gives good gifts: Lord, have mercy. Christ, you are the Savior who promised to set us free: Christ, have mercy. Lord, you are the Spirit who dwells within us: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people.
homily:
We have all known that specific, hollow ache of the midnight hour. It is the time when the world goes quiet, when the distractions of the day fall away, and the heart is left alone with its own questions. In today’s Gospel, Jesus gives us a startling image: a man knocking at a friend’s door at midnight, asking for bread. It is a scene of persistence, of a need that cannot wait until morning. The man is not asking for luxury. He is not asking for a miracle of gold or fame. He is asking for bread, the most basic, essential sustenance for a guest who has arrived from a long journey. He is asking because he is empty, and he has nothing to offer to those he loves.

How often have we stood at that same door? We come to the Father with our own empty hands. We come seeking comfort, seeking clarity, seeking the strength to carry on when the weight feels like more than we can bear. We look at the life of our dear Benjamin Vo, a boy whose very existence was a gift of light, and we feel that same hunger—the hunger to understand, the hunger to hold, the hunger to have him here with us again. We knock on the door of heaven, sometimes with a gentle tap, sometimes with a desperate, pounding fist, asking, 'Lord, I have nothing to offer this day. I have no bread for this journey. Help me.'

Saint Paul, in his letter to the Galatians, is quite blunt. He asks, 'Did you receive the Spirit from works of the law, or from faith in what you heard?' He is trying to shake his people awake, to remind them that God’s love is not a reward for our perfection or a wage we earn by doing everything right. It is a gift we receive through faith. It is a relationship. It is the breath of the Spirit that moves through us, regardless of how tired we are or how broken we feel. Paul is calling them back to the simplicity of the beginning: it is all grace.

Think of Benjamin. Think of that brilliant, curious mind of his. He was a boy who loved the mechanics of how things worked—the code in his GitHub repositories, the complex systems of the world, the sheer, soaring wonder of aviation. He was a builder. He loved to create. But the true beauty of Benjamin was not in what he achieved, but in the gentle, open-handed way he moved through his fifteen years. He was a boy who looked at the world and saw a place to be kind. Remember that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his Uncle William? He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, he didn't need to count the coins. The offer itself was the truth of his heart. It was a heart that knew, instinctively, that we are here to give.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these past three months, the silence of the house has sometimes felt like a wall. You remember the way Ben would talk about his 'con chim airlines'—that dream he had, the way he would giggle and smile, his eyes bright with the possibility of flight. He was a boy who was always looking up. He was a boy who loved the stories his father told, who shared the quiet, steady bond with his brother, Ryan. You gave him a home where he was free to be curious, free to be brilliant, and free to be gentle. And that love you gave him did not vanish when he went home to God. It is still moving. It is still working. It is the very thing that connects you to him even now.

There is a temptation to think that if we are 'good' enough, or if we pray hard enough, the door will open exactly the way we want it to. But Jesus says something deeper. He says, 'What father among you would hand his son a snake when he asks for a fish?' He is telling us that the Father in heaven is not a distant, stingy neighbor who has to be badgered into kindness. He is the One who knows exactly what we need, even before we ask. He is the One who gives us the Holy Spirit, the very life of God Himself, to dwell within us. That is the bread we are given at midnight. It is not always the bread we thought we wanted, but it is the bread that sustains the soul.

Ryan, you are the one who carries that legacy of curiosity and kindness. You know the rhythm of Ben’s heart better than anyone. When you see a plane climbing into the clouds, or when you sit down to code, or when you just look at the world with that same wonder you both shared, know that you are not doing it alone. You are a family of four. That is an eternal truth. The geography of your life has changed, but the bond of your love is held by the One who loves you both with an everlasting love. Keep being the brother who reaches out. Keep being the boy who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that visits you in the quiet of the night. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of wondering if they missed something, if they could have done more, if they could have changed the outcome. I want to lift that stone from you today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

We are on this earth to be witnesses to the love that does not die. Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, that well dedicated in Ben’s name. It is a perfect image of his life. It is not a monument to the past; it is a source of life for the present. It is water for the thirsty. It is a sign that the kindness he carried is still flowing, still reaching, still refreshing the world. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

When the days feel long and the silence feels heavy, remember that you are not being asked to understand the mysteries of the universe. You are being asked to trust the One who holds the stars in place and who holds Benjamin in the palm of His hand. You are being asked to live in such a way that his memory continues to be a blessing to everyone you meet. You are not walking in the dark. You are walking in the light of the Resurrection.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest in the light of Christ and find their home in the Banquet of Heaven, we pray to the Lord.

For all who grieve, especially Alan, Thao, and Ryan, that the God of all consolation may hold them close, dry every tear, and grant them the strength and hope to continue living in the light of His love, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
O stupid Galatians!
Who has bewitched you,
before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified?
I want to learn only this from you:
did you receive the Spirit from works of the law,
or from faith in what you heard?
Are you so stupid?
After beginning with the Spirit,
are you now ending with the flesh?
Did you experience so many things in vain?–
if indeed it was in vain.
Does, then, the one who supplies the Spirit to you
and works mighty deeds among you
do so from works of the law
or from faith in what you heard?

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (68) Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people.
He has raised up for us a mighty savior,
born of the house of his servant David.
R. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people.
Through his holy prophets he promised of old
that he would save us from our enemies,
from the hands of all who hate us.
R. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people.
He promised to show mercy to our fathers
and to remember his holy covenant.
R. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people.
This was the oath he swore to our father Abraham:
to set us free from the hands of our enemies,
free to worship him without fear,
holy and righteous in his sight
all the days of our life.
R. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; He has come to his people.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
“Suppose one of you has a friend
to whom he goes at midnight and says,
‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
for a friend of mine has arrived at my house from a journey
and I have nothing to offer him,’
and he says in reply from within,
‘Do not bother me; the door has already been locked
and my children and I are already in bed.
I cannot get up to give you anything.’
I tell you, if he does not get up to give him the loaves
because of their friendship,
he will get up to give him whatever he needs
because of his persistence.“And I tell you, ask and you will receive;
seek and you will find;
knock and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks, receives;
and the one who seeks, finds;
and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
What father  among you would hand his son a snake
when he asks for a fish?
Or hand him a scorpion when he asks for an egg?
If you then, who are wicked,
know how to give good gifts to your children,
how much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit
to those who ask him?”

day: Thursday of the Twenty-seventh Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
